subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your grandparents why switching off the fan matters, and give two easy ways your family can save energy.
prompt_hi: Apne dada-dadi ya nana-nani ko samjhao ki pankha band karna kyon zaroori hai, aur family ke liye energy bachaane ke do aasaan tareeke batao.
answer: Much electricity is made by burning coal, which runs out and pollutes the air; small savings add up across homes. Easy ways: switch off when leaving a room, use LEDs, use daylight, switch off at the wall, walk or cycle for short trips.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: name one energy source that will run out and one that won't.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: energy ka ek srot batao jo khatam ho jayega aur ek jo nahi hoga.
answer: Will run out: coal, petrol, diesel or LPG. Won't run out: sunlight, wind or flowing water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Put these steps in order for making cotton cloth: weaving, picking the cotton, spinning into thread, removing the seeds.
prompt_hi: Cotton ka kapda banaane ke ye steps sahi kram mein lagao: bunaai (weaving), kapaas todna, kaat ke dhaaga banana (spinning), beej nikaalna.
answer: Picking the cotton, removing the seeds, spinning into thread, then weaving into cloth.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Take a little cotton wool from the first-aid box. Pull out a few loose fibres and tug them gently. Now twist some fibres tightly between your fingers into a thread and tug again. Predict first: which will break more easily?
prompt_hi: First-aid box se thodi rui lo. Kuch dheele reshe nikaalo aur halke se kheencho. Ab kuch reshon ko ungliyon ke beech kas ke batt ke dhaaga banao aur phir kheencho. Pehle guess karo: kaun jaldi tootega?
answer: The loose, untwisted fibres pull apart easily; the twisted thread is much stronger. Spinning twists many short fibres together to make strong yarn.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Take an old cotton handkerchief or a scrap of cloth (ask first). Gently pull a thread out from its edge with your fingers. Predict: what pattern of threads will you see if you look closely, or with a magnifying glass?
prompt_hi: Ek purana cotton rumaal ya kapde ka tukda lo (pehle poochh lena). Kinaare se ungliyon se dheere se ek dhaaga kheencho. Guess karo: paas se ya magnifying glass se dekhoge toh dhaagon ka kaisa pattern dikhega?
answer: Two sets of threads crossing each other at right angles, going over and under one another; that is weaving.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A weaver at a handloom may take many days, sometimes weeks, to weave one rich Kanchipuram silk saree, while a factory power loom makes plain cloth very fast. Predict: which will usually cost more, and why?
prompt_hi: Handloom pe ek bunkar ko ek bhaari Kanchipuram silk saree bunne mein kai din, kabhi-kabhi hafte lag jaate hain, jabki factory ka power loom saadha kapda bahut jaldi bana deta hai. Guess karo: kaunsa aam taur pe zyada mehenga hoga, aur kyon?
answer: The handwoven silk saree. Silk fibre is costly, and the weaver's skill and many days of handwork go into each one, while machines make plain cloth quickly in large amounts.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why do we twist (spin) cotton fibres before weaving them?
prompt_hi: Bunne se pehle hum cotton ke reshon ko batt ke (spin karke) dhaaga kyon banaate hain?
answer: Single fibres are short and weak; twisting many together makes a long, strong thread that can be woven.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why did Gandhiji ask people to spin on the charkha and wear khadi?
prompt_hi: Gandhiji ne logon ko charkha chalaane aur khadi pehenne ko kyon kaha?
answer: So that Indians could make their own cloth by hand instead of buying cloth from British factories; it gave work to villagers and was a sign of self-reliance during the freedom struggle.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare how we get cotton and silk: where does each fibre come from, and how is the thread taken out?
prompt_hi: Cotton aur silk kaise milte hain, unki tulna karo: dono resha kahaan se aata hai, aur dhaaga kaise nikaala jaata hai?
answer: Cotton comes from the fluffy fibres around the seeds of the cotton plant; it is picked, the seeds are removed, and the short fibres are spun into thread. Silk comes from the cocoon of the silkworm, which feeds on mulberry leaves; a cocoon is one very long thread, which is unwound (reeled) after the cocoon is softened in hot water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Look at the labels inside three clothes at home. What are they made of: cotton, silk, wool, polyester, or a mix? Which come from plants, which from animals, and which are made from chemicals in factories?
prompt_hi: Ghar ke 3 kapdon ke andar ka label dekho. Woh kis cheez ke bane hain: cotton, silk, wool, polyester ya mix? Kaun paudhon se, kaun jaanwaron se, aur kaun factory mein chemicals se bane hain?
answer: Answers vary. Cotton comes from plants; silk and wool come from animals; polyester and nylon are synthetic fibres made in factories from chemicals.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Jute bags are made in West Bengal. Why might a shop choose jute bags instead of plastic bags?
prompt_hi: Jute ke thaile West Bengal mein bante hain. Koi dukaan plastic ki thaili ki jagah jute ke thaile kyon chunegi?
answer: Jute is a strong plant fibre; jute bags can be reused many times and rot away naturally when thrown away, while plastic lasts hundreds of years. Jute also gives work to farmers and weavers.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Tear two sheets of different-coloured paper into strips with your hands (no scissors). Weave the strips over and under like a mat. Then draw what you made and label the strips going one way and the other.
prompt_hi: Do alag rang ke kaagaz ko haath se patti-patti phaad lo (kainchi nahi). Pattiyon ko chatai jaise upar-neeche bun lo. Phir jo banaya uski drawing banao aur ek taraf aur doosri taraf jaane wali pattiyon ko label karo.
answer: A checkerboard pattern: one set of strips runs lengthwise, like the warp, and the other goes across, over and under, like the weft; this is how threads are woven into cloth.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Pinky says, 'Silk comes from the silk cotton tree, and wool comes from the cotton plant.' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Pinky kehti hai, 'Resham semal (silk cotton) ke ped se aata hai, aur oon kapaas ke paudhe se.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Silk comes from the cocoon of the silkworm, an insect, and wool from the hair of sheep, goats and some other animals. Cotton and jute are the plant fibres; the silk cotton tree gives a fluffy fibre, but not silk.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how a cotton shirt was made, all the way from a cotton field.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki cotton ki shirt kaise bani, kapaas ke khet se lekar shirt tak.
answer: Cotton grows in bolls in the field; it is picked, the seeds are removed, the fibres are cleaned, spun (twisted) into thread, woven into cloth on a handloom or in a factory, dyed, and then cut and stitched into a shirt.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: what is spinning, and what is weaving?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: spinning kya hai, aur weaving kya hai?
answer: Spinning is twisting fibres together into thread; weaving is crossing two sets of threads over and under to make cloth.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Name three things you can make from old clothes.
prompt_hi: Purane kapdon se 3 cheezein batao jo bana sakte hain.
answer: Any three: a quilt (kantha or godhadi), a bag, a duster or pochha, a cushion cover, a doormat, patchwork, a rag doll, hair bands.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Lay a piece of dark coloured old cloth in a sunny window and cover half of it with a piece of cardboard. Leave it for two or three weeks. Predict: what will the two halves look like?
prompt_hi: Gehre rang ka purana kapde ka tukda dhoop wali khidki pe rakho aur uska aadha hissa gatte se dhak do. Do-teen hafte chhod do. Guess karo: dono hisse kaise dikhenge?
answer: The uncovered half fades and becomes lighter; the covered half keeps its colour. Strong sunlight fades dyes, so coloured clothes are dried in shade or inside out.

subject: evs
prompt_en: With an adult, wet two old handkerchiefs. Fold one and keep it inside a closed box; hang the other open in a breezy place. Predict: after two days, which one will show spots or a musty smell? To check, the adult opens the box while you look from a little distance: do not sniff close or touch any spots. Then the adult seals that cloth in a bag for the bin, and everyone washes hands.
prompt_hi: Kisi bade ke saath do purane rumaal geele karo. Ek ko tah karke band dibbe mein rakho; doosre ko hawa wali jagah khula taang do. Guess karo: do din baad kaunse pe dhabbe dikhenge ya seelan ki smell aayegi? Check karte waqt dibba bada khole aur tum thodi door se dekho: paas se soongho mat, dhabbe chhoona mat. Phir bada us rumaal ko band thaili mein karke kachre mein daale, aur sab haath dho lein.
answer: The one in the closed box: it stays damp and warm with no air, so mould (microbes) grows on it; the hanging one dries and stays fresh.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Make a lacing card: an adult punches two rows of holes in thick cardboard. With a shoelace, lace a running stitch on one row and a back stitch on the other. Predict first: which row will have gaps, and which will hold two cardboard pieces together better?
prompt_hi: Lacing card banao: koi bada mote gatte mein chhedon ki do lines bana de. Joote ke feete se ek line pe running stitch aur doosri pe back stitch karo. Pehle guess karo: kis line mein gap honge, aur kaunsi do gatte ke tukdon ko zyada mazbooti se jodegi?
answer: The running-stitch row has gaps and holds less firmly; the back-stitch row has no gaps and holds better.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why should we mend a small tear in clothes quickly instead of waiting?
prompt_hi: Kapde mein chhota sa ched ho toh use jaldi kyon silna chahiye, intezaar kyon nahi karna chahiye?
answer: A small tear gets bigger every time the cloth is pulled or washed; mending it early is quick and saves the clothes.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why is reusing old clothes good for the Earth?
prompt_hi: Purane kapdon ko dobara use karna dharti ke liye achha kyon hai?
answer: Making new cloth uses water, energy, land and dyes; reusing means less new cloth has to be made and less waste goes to dumps, where synthetic clothes do not rot.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare two ways to deal with a bundle of old cotton sarees: (A) throw them in the garbage; (B) stitch them into a quilt like a kantha or godhadi. What is gained or lost in each?
prompt_hi: Purani cotton sareeyon ke bundle ke do istemaal ki tulna karo: (A) kachre mein phenk dena; (B) unse kantha ya godhadi jaisi rajai silna. Dono mein kya milta hai ya kya khota hai?
answer: A: the cloth is wasted and goes to a dump. B: the family gets a warm, useful quilt, keeps memories of the sarees, needs no new cloth, and keeps a traditional craft alive.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A button has come off your school shirt. Make a plan to fix it safely.
prompt_hi: Tumhari school shirt ka button toot ke gir gaya hai. Ise surakshit tareeke se theek karne ka plan banao.
answer: Keep the button safe; ask an adult to help or to sew it while you watch; thread a needle, sew through the button's holes several times, and tie a knot at the back.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your class wants to start a 'clothes bank' for winter. Plan how to collect, check and share old clothes.
prompt_hi: Tumhari class sardi ke liye ek 'clothes bank' shuru karna chahti hai. Purane kapde ikattha karne, jaanchne aur baantne ka plan banao.
answer: Collect clean clothes from families; sort them by size and season; mend small tears and sew on buttons with adult help; wash and fold them; share them with people who need them through a local group or the school; keep a simple record.

subject: evs
prompt_en: On paper, draw a running stitch and a back stitch as lines of dashes. Show where the thread goes on the front and behind the cloth.
prompt_hi: Kaagaz pe running stitch aur back stitch ko dash wali lines ki tarah banao. Dikhao ki dhaaga kapde ke aage kahaan hai aur peeche kahaan.
answer: Running stitch: dash, gap, dash, gap, with the thread passing behind the cloth at each gap. Back stitch: dashes touching end to end with no gaps, the thread going back to the end of the previous stitch and then forward underneath.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Bunty says, 'Always dry every cloth in the hottest sun for the whole day. That's how to care for clothes.' What would you tell him?
prompt_hi: Bunty kehta hai, 'Har kapde ko hamesha poore din sabse tez dhoop mein sukhaao. Yahi kapdon ki dekhbhaal hai.' Tum use kya bologe?
answer: Sun is good for drying and freshness, but strong sun for a long time fades coloured clothes and can harm wool and silk; dry coloured clothes in shade or inside out, and take them in once dry.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your friend three ways to make clothes last longer and two ways to reuse them when they get old.
prompt_hi: Apne dost ko samjhao ki kapdon ko zyada din chalaane ke 3 tareeke kya hain, aur purane hone pe unhe dobara use karne ke do tareeke kya hain.
answer: Last longer: wash gently, dry coloured clothes in shade or inside out, store them only when fully dry, mend tears early. Reuse: quilts, bags, dusters, cushion covers, or give them to someone who needs them.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: which stitch leaves gaps between the stitches?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kaunsi silaai mein taankon ke beech gap rehta hai?
answer: The running stitch.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In which direction does the Sun rise, and in which direction does it set?
prompt_hi: Suraj kis disha mein ugta hai, aur kis disha mein doobta hai?
answer: It rises in the east and sets in the west.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In a dark room, shine a torch on a ball or globe and stick a small paper dot on India. Predict: as you slowly turn the ball, when will India be in light and when in dark? Will the torch ever have to 'go behind' anything?
prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein ek ball ya globe pe torch daalo aur India pe kaagaz ka chhota sa dot chipkao. Guess karo: ball ko dheere-dheere ghumaane pe India kab roshni mein hoga aur kab andhere mein? Kya torch ko kabhi kisi cheez ke 'peeche jaana' padega?
answer: India is lit while it faces the torch (day) and dark when it turns away (night); the torch keeps shining all the time and never moves or hides. Only the ball's turning brings day and night.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Predict: if the Earth suddenly stopped spinning, what would happen to day and night where you live?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar Prithvi achaanak ghoomna band kar de, toh tumhari jagah din aur raat ka kya hoga?
answer: Day and night would become very, very long: the side facing the Sun would stay in daylight for months, and the other side would stay dark for months.

subject: evs
prompt_en: At morning school assembly, you stand with your back to the Sun. Predict: which direction will your shadow point, east or west? And which way will it point in the evening?
prompt_hi: Subah school assembly mein tum Suraj ki taraf peeth karke khade ho. Guess karo: tumhari parchhaai kis disha mein hogi, purab ya paschim? Aur shaam ko kis taraf hogi?
answer: In the morning the Sun is in the east, so your shadow points west; in the evening the Sun is in the west, so your shadow points east. A shadow forms where your body blocks the sunlight.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why does the Sun seem to rise in the east, even though it is the Earth that moves?
prompt_hi: Jab Prithvi ghoomti hai, toh Suraj purab se ugta hua kyon dikhta hai?
answer: The Earth spins from west to east. As our place turns towards the Sun, the Sun first comes into view on the eastern horizon, and later it disappears from view in the west, just as trees seem to rush backwards when you look out of a moving train.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why is it dark at night even on a clear night with no clouds at all?
prompt_hi: Bilkul saaf, bina baadal wali raat mein bhi andhera kyon hota hai?
answer: Because our side of the Earth has turned away from the Sun; clouds or the Moon are not blocking it.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Sitting in a moving train, the trees outside seem to rush backwards. Compare this with the Sun seeming to move across the sky. What is really moving in each case?
prompt_hi: Chalti train mein baithe hue bahar ke ped peeche bhaagte lagte hain. Isse Suraj ke aasmaan mein chalte dikhne ki tulna karo. Dono mein asal mein kya chal raha hai?
answer: In the train, the trees stay still and the train moves; in the sky, the Sun does not go around us each day, the Earth turns, which makes the Sun appear to move from east to west.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your cousin in Dubai video-calls you at 8 pm in India. About what time is it there, and is it day or evening? What about your uncle in the USA: morning or night?
prompt_hi: Dubai mein rehne wala tumhara cousin India ke raat 8 baje video call karta hai. Wahaan lagbhag kitne baje honge, din hai ya shaam? Aur USA wale chacha ke yahaan: subah hai ya raat?
answer: Dubai is a little to the west of India and about one and a half hours behind, so it is about 6:30 pm there: early evening. Whether the Sun has already set depends on the season: still light in summer, already dark in winter. The USA is on the far side of the Earth, so it is morning there.

subject: evs
prompt_en: An astronaut on the space station looks at the Earth from far away. What would she see on the side facing the Sun and on the side away from it?
prompt_hi: Space station pe ek astronaut door se Prithvi ko dekhti hai. Use Suraj ki taraf wale hisse pe aur doosri taraf wale hisse pe kya dikhega?
answer: She would see one half lit by sunlight, having day, and the other half dark, having night, with city lights twinkling; along the line between them, places are having sunrise or sunset.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw the Sun on one side and the Earth as a circle. Shade the night half and mark India in daylight. Then draw it again 12 hours later.
prompt_hi: Ek taraf Suraj aur ek gola Prithvi ka banao. Raat wala aadha hissa shade karo aur India ko din wale hisse mein dikhao. Phir 12 ghante baad ki drawing dobara banao.
answer: First drawing: India on the lit half facing the Sun. Second drawing: India on the dark half, away from the Sun. The Sun stays in the same place in both.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says, 'At night the Sun goes to sleep behind the mountains.' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai, 'Raat ko Suraj pahadon ke peeche so jaata hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: The Sun never goes behind the mountains or sleeps; it keeps shining. Our side of the Earth turns away from it, so we have night while the other side has day.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to a little child, using a torch and a ball, why we have day and night.
prompt_hi: Torch aur ball ki madad se ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki din aur raat kyon hote hain.
answer: The torch is the Sun and the ball is the Earth. The Earth spins once in about 24 hours; the side facing the Sun has day and the side away has night. The Sun does not move around us or hide; the Earth's turning makes it seem to rise in the east and set in the west.
